etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English surfeite, surfet, a borrowing from Anglo-Norman surfet, surfeit and Old French sorfet, sorfait, past participle of surfaire (“to augment, exaggerate, exceed”), from sur- (“over”) + faire (“to do”). The adjective is derived from the noun.
senses: (uncountable) Overindulgence in either food or drink; overeating.
(transitive) To feed (someone) to excess (on, upon or with something).
